quotes.text: Here's something important to understand. Security and dataverse is additive, not subtractive. If a user has two roles, they get the most permissive access from either role.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains a frequently misunderstood rule of Dataverse security that drives role design.

quotes.text: The golden rule of dataverse security is this, don't assign system administrator to everyone. That role gives full access to everything in the environment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable least-privilege recommendation for Dataverse admins.

quotes.text: SharePoint is a collaboration platform that happens to have lists. Dataverse is a proper relational database, built from the ground up for business apps.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the core difference between the two platforms in two sentences.

quotes.text: Use Dataverse for your structured data, customers, orders, products, the things that need relationships and security. Use SharePoint for documents.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear hybrid architecture pattern for business apps.

quotes.text: Plan your data model on paper before you start building. Draw the tables, draw the relationships, figure out who needs to see what. A few hours of planning can save you weeks of rework.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical advice that prevents costly redesigns.

chapters.title: Role-based security, business units and teams
Getting started with your data model

takeaways: Dataverse is a managed relational data platform that handles tables, relationships, security and business logic so every Power Platform app, flow and report shares one foundation.
Lookup columns, enforced referential integrity and role-based security with business units, teams and column-level security make Dataverse far more robust than spreadsheets or SharePoint lists.
Use SharePoint for simple trackers and documents, choose Dataverse for business-critical systems of record, and start with standard tables and a data model planned on paper.
hook: Still running business data on Excel files and SharePoint lists that hit the 5,000-item wall? This episode explains Dataverse in plain English for Power Platform makers and IT pros: tables, relationships, role-based security and how Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI build on it. You will know when Dataverse is the right foundation and how to start your first data model.
